messages:
sana: noticing a cluster of 'invalid_client' OIDC errors from the web app starting ~08:07 UTC. New hires can't SSO in. Seeing 401s from oidc/token endpoint.

ben: I saw that too, correlate with secret-manager activity around 07:55. There was an automated secret rotation for client_id=app-web-ui via compliance-runner.

kai: quick check -> scim sync jobs show 401s as well when fetching /Groups; token_exchange failing. sample log: `oauth2.token error=invalid_client client_id=app-web-ui grant=refresh_token`

ben: hmm the rotation job was supposed to distribute new client secret to the SCIM connector. Looks like the connector missed the update (stale env). Could be because the deployment didn't pick up the new mount.

sana: audit-bot: can you surface the secret rotation event and who triggered it?

audit-bot: [audit] secret.rotate invoked user=security-ci pipeline=compliance-runner secret=secrets/clients/app-web-ui at=2025-03-11T07:55:22Z

kai: found the root cause in the connector pod logs: `failed to refresh secret: mount path not found` 1: the k8s projected volume was not attached after the pod restart because node kubelet had an intermittent CSI timeout. Some replicas picked it up, others didn't -> partial auth failures and racey deprovisions.

ben: partial auths explain intermittent UI SSO failures. But I also see a bigger problem: during the partial failure window the sync job retried and, due to an outdated ACL rule, one retry executed a DELETE of a service account that matched a pattern (staging-*) used by infra.

sana: wait, we just lost a staging service account? Which one and what was the impact?

kai: deleted acct: svc-stg-deployer-42. It had a limited role but held a renewal token used by a non-critical deploy pipeline. That pipeline failed and retried; no customer impact.

ben: still bad. We need three things now: 1) restore the deleted service account and token 2) reconcile SCIM state to avoid further deletes 3) prevent secret rotations from causing this without explicit operator approval.

sana: restoring: I re-created svc-stg-deployer-42 and re-issued a new token using the recovery playbook. Deploys resumed. Marking as recovered.

kai: reconciliation: paused SCIM automatic delete-on-absent for 30m and kicked off a full list-sync to compare IdP<->our users/groups.

ben: for the rotation guard I propose: a) require a 'rotation-review' flag for client secrets tied to provisioning roles, b) add a pre-rotation hook that verifies downstream consumers are healthy (healthcheck for scim connector), c) add an alert when oauth2.invalid_client error rate > 5/m.

sana: +1 on all. Also logging: add a more granular audit entry when a SCIM delete is initiated that captures the 'initiator-client' and last-2 sync diffs. We had only high-level delete logs which made debugging slower.

audit-bot: [note] created ticket SECURITY-2025: "Guarded client secret rotation for provisioning clients" assigned to ben.

pagerduty: incident acknowledged by oncall @kai. PagerDuty: INC-98723 created severity=low reason="non-prod svcacct deleted during client rotation".

kai: follow-ups: 1) add a kubelet CSI timeout monitor by node to surface secret mount failures 2) make SCIM deletes require two-step confirmation for principals with role in [deployers, infra] 3) add a runbook entry for rapid recreate of service accounts with audit-proofing.

ben: I'll open PRs: one to add the rotation-review flag + pre-rotation healthcheck; another to change SCIM delete semantics for privileged roles.

sana: also add a vuln triage note: the compliance pipeline currently can rotate client secrets without an express human approval for service accounts that control provisioning. Let's mark that as medium and block automatic rotation for those secrets until locked down.

audit-bot: [audit] scim.pause_delete initiated user=sana pause_until=2025-03-11T09:00:00Z

kai: smoke checks: SSO flows green on canaries for 10m, scim list-sync completed no further deletes.

sana: closing thread once PRs are merged and alerts are in place. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
